main_topics.reason: The user came because of new zigzag lights before a migraine and the first several turns cover describing and interpreting it.
The user was scared and asked whether aura could signal stroke; later said they felt calmer after their hands had been shaking.
The user wanted to know whether to go to the ER tonight or wait, and asked for confirmation that they did not need to rush.
The user asked whether aura will now be a permanent new feature.
The user asked how to tell if the disturbance affects one eye or both, and the bot gave a practical test.
The user asked about using aura as an early cue to take sumatriptan, which took a couple of turns.
The user raised the aura and birth control link and engaged with the answer for two turns.
The bot summarised points to raise with the family doctor and the user planned to book an appointment.

output.summary: A user with years of migraines described a first-time shimmering zigzag visual disturbance lasting about 20 minutes before a headache and asked whether it could be a stroke or an emergency. The bot explained it fits migraine aura, gave red-flag guardrails, advised a non-urgent doctor visit, and covered sumatriptan timing and the aura-estrogen contraception caution. The user said they felt much calmer and planned to book with their family doctor this week and rest tonight.
